text:
alex: Heads up — saw a p95 spike on Mistral-7B sliding-window inference after we enabled longer contexts. root cause looks like kernel chooser oscillating between fast matmul and fallbacks, causing KV cache pointer churn. profiler attached below.
maria: link? rough numbers?
alex: p95 went from 110ms -> 420ms for seq_len=4096 with mixed prefix lengths. CPU/GPU kernels switching mid-session. profiler snippet:
```
kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_v2 -> fallback=matmul_safe
kv_ptr_updates: 923 -> 4120/sec
batch_compactions: 18 -> 103
```
sean: Are you using max_position_embeddings override? Mistral has RoPE quirks — if effective_pos > model_pos we apply scaling which flips kernel tiling heuristics.
alex: yes, we set max_position_embeddings=4096 at runtime. I think RoPE scaling triggers extra remap every time we cross window boundary with sliding attention.
kai: Observed something similar last week. Two actionable ideas:
- Add a cooldown to kernel selector when a session's kv_cache pointer pattern shows sliding-window signatures (i.e., repeating KV reuse).
- Group batches by "recent_prefix_len" in the batching heuristic so we avoid mixing warm/hot caches in the same GPU batch.
maria: grouping sounds promising. Any perf numbers for cooldown?
alex: quick A/B test:
```
baseline: p95=420ms, p50=120ms, tokens/sec=78
cooldown:  p95=160ms, p50=125ms, tokens/sec=210
grouping:  p95=140ms, p50=110ms, tokens/sec=230
combined:  p95=115ms, p50=105ms, tokens/sec=260
```
perf-bot: :speedboat: CI microbench run 1793004319 finished — 7/8 tests passed (one flaky mem leak).
sean: Nice. For RoPE scaling we should avoid full remap by using lazy scaled offsets — only recompute on boundary crossing rather than per-token. That should reduce kv_ptr churn.
alex: I prototyped lazy remap; CPU overhead small. Implementation diff:
```
if window_crossed(session):
    remap_rope_offsets()
else:
    use_cached_offsets()
```
kai: Also check kernel tile sizes — mats of dim 64 vs 128 show different fallback rates on Ampere. Maybe prefer 64 for sequences with many small prefixes.
maria: Let's do a canary rollout on dedicated pool A, feature flag `slide-window-kernel-cooldown=v1`. I'll handle the rollout and monitoring dashboard.
alex: I'll open a perf PR with tests + the grouping change. Will add a regression eval to Redwood Optimize to catch this pattern.
sean: FYI we should add a small synthetic eval: mix of short (<=128) and long (>=2048) prefixes to exercise the mix batching.
maria: @alex @sean @kai added to the canary, assigning follow-ups:
- alex: PR + perf results (due EOD)
- kai: kernel tiling analysis (tomorrow)
- sean: eval harness + synthetic test (this week)
alex: thanks — tagging this thread into eng-runtime docs for future reference. :memo:
